spots.name: Nidaros Cathedral
spots.summary: Nidaros Cathedral is a Church of Norway cathedral located in the city of Trondheim in Trøndelag county. It is built over the burial site of King Olav II, who brought Christianity to Norway and became the patron saint of the nation; the consecration of new Norwegian monarchs occurs at Nidaros Cathedral.

spots.name: Stiftsgården
spots.summary: Stiftsgården is the royal residence in Trondheim, Norway. It is centrally situated on the city’s most important thoroughfare, Munkegaten. At 140 rooms constituting 4000 m² (43000 ft²), it is one of the largest wooden buildings in Northern Europe, and it has been used by royalty and their guests since 1800.

spots.name: Old Town Bridge
spots.summary: Old Town Bridge is located in Trondheim, Trøndelag County, Norway.

spots.name: Vår Frue Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Vår Frue Church is a medieval parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the downtown Midtbyen area of the city of Trondheim, just a few blocks north of the Nidaros Cathedral.

spots.name: Olav Tryggvason
spots.summary: A statue of Olav Tryggvason is located in Trondheim, Norway. Sculpted by sculptor Wilhelm Rasmussen, it honors King Olav Tryggvason, who was the city's founder.

spots.name: Kristiansten Fortress
spots.summary: Kristiansten Fortress is located on a hill east of the city of Trondheim which is located within Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway, named after Christian V of Denmark-Norway. It was built after the city fire of Trondheim in 1681 to protect the city against attack from the east.

spots.name: Archbishop's Palace, Trondheim

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Archbishop's Palace in Trondheim is a castle and palace in the city of Trondheim, located just south of the Nidaros Cathedral. For hundreds of years, the castle was the seat, residence and administrative center of the Archbishop of Nidaros.

spots.name: Tyholttårnet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tyholttårnet is a 124-metre (407 ft) tall radio tower with an observation deck in Trondheim, Norway. It was completed in 1985. The tower features the Egon revolving restaurant, at an altitude of 74 metres (243 ft), which makes one complete revolution per hour.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Trondheim Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Trondheim Synagogue is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at Arkitekt Christies gate 1B, in Trondheim, Norway. Established as a congregation in June 1892, the present synagogue has served the Jewish community since its inauguration on October 13, 1925.

spots.name: Trondheim Cathedral School
spots.summary: Trondheim Cathedral School is an upper secondary school located next to the Nidaros Cathedral in the center of Trondheim, Norway. The school has an enrollment of 596 and the current Head of school is Tor Bitusøyl.

spots.name: St. Olav's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. Olav's Cathedral is the church home to the Prelature of Trondheim, belonging to the Catholic Church in Norway.

spots.name: Rockheim
spots.summary: Rockheim is Norway's national museum for popular music from the 1950s to the present. It is a division of Museene i Sør-Trøndelag and is housed in a former grain warehouse in Trondheim. It opened in 2010; since 2013, the director has been Sissel Guttormsen.

spots.name: NTNU University Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The NTNU University Museum in Trondheim is one of seven Norwegian university museums with natural and cultural history collections and exhibits. The museum has research and administrative responsibility over archaeology and biology in Central Norway.

spots.name: Skansen Bridge
spots.summary: The Skansen Bridge is a 52-meter span fixed-trunnion bascule railway bridge located at Skansen in Trondheim, Norway.

spots.name: Elgeseter Bridge
spots.summary: Elgeseter Bridge is a bridge in the city and municipality of Trondheim in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is part of the European route E6 highway which passes over the Nidelva river and connects Prinsens street in the Midtbyen area of Trondheim with Elgeseter street in the Elgeseter area of Trondheim in the south.

spots.name: Trøndelag Teater
spots.summary: Trøndelag Teater is a large theater in the city of Trondheim, in Trøndelag county, Norway.

spots.name: Trondheim Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Trondheim Art Museum is an art museum located in Trondheim in Sør-Trøndelag county, Norway. The museum shows temporary exhibitions of international and regional art in dialogue with works from the museum's collection.

spots.name: Helgeseter Priory

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Helgeseter Priory or Elgeseter Priory was a medieval era house of Augustinian Canons in what is now the neighborhood of Elgeseter in Trondheim, Norway.

spots.name: Rustkammeret
spots.summary: "The Armoury" Army Museum in Trondheim is a military museum in the Archbishop's Palace (Erkebispegården) in Trondheim, Norway. Today it is a Norwegian army museum as well as a resistance museum, emphasizing the military history of Trøndelag.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Pirbadet
spots.summary: Pirbadet is a combined indoor water park and public pool in Trondheim, Norway, which opened in 2001. As of 2025, it is one of only two publicly open pools in Trondheim, the other being Husebybadet.

spots.name: Lade Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lade Church is one of Norway's oldest existing stone churches. It is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the Lade neighborhood in the city of Trondheim, just southeast of Korsvika and east of Ladehammeren.

spots.name: Bakke Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bakke Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the Bakklandet area of the city of Trondheim, and the church serves the Bakklandet, Møllenberg, Rosenborg, and Nedre Elvehavn areas of Østbyen in Trondheim.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.name: Ilen Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ilen Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the Ila area in the city of Trondheim, on the 250-metre (820 ft) wide isthmus between the river Nid and the Trondheimsfjord.

spots.name: Strinda Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Strinda Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the Strinda area in the city of Trondheim. It is the church for the Strinda parish which is part of the Strinda prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros.

spots.name: Trondheim Science Museum
spots.summary: Trondheim Science Centre is located in the Kongens gate area of Trondheim, Norway.

spots.name: Lerkendal Stadion
spots.summary: The Lerkendal Stadion is an all-seater association football stadium located at Lerkendal in Trondheim, Norway. The home ground of the Eliteserien (2017) side Rosenborg BK, it has a capacity for 21,405 spectators, making it the second-largest football stadium in the country.

spots.name: Norwegian National Museum of Justice

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Norwegian National Museum of Justice is a public museum of penal justice and law enforcement in Trondheim, Norway. It is housed in a former prison. From 2001-2017, the director of the museum was Johan Sigfred Helberg. From 2017-2018, the director was Brynja Birgisdottir and since 2019, has been Åshild Karevold.

spots.name: Nidarholm Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nidarholm Abbey was a Benedictine monastery located on the island of Munkholmen in Trondheim Fjord on the sea approach to Trondheim, Norway.

spots.name: Ringve Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Ringve Museum is Norway's national museum for music and musical instruments, with collections from all over the world.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Verftsbrua
spots.summary: Verftsbrua, also popularly called Blomsterbrua, is a bridge at the bay of Trondheim. The bridge, built in 2003, spans 125 metres (410 ft). The name Verftsbrua comes from the nearby shipyard, Trondhjems mekaniske Værksted, while the name Blomsterbrua is due to the bridge featuring flowerbeds along its edges.

photo.author: Municipal Archives of Trondheim from Trondheim, Norway

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Norsk Døvemuseum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: Norsk Døvemuseum is a museum in Trondheim, Norway. It is a division of Trøndelag Folkemuseum. The museum is located in Rødbygget, which was drawn by Christian Heinrich Grosch. It was the first Neo-Gothic building in Trondheim, built in 1855. The museum was established in 1992, and rebuilt in 2009.

spots.name: Trondheim gamle rådhus
spots.summary: The city library is built upon the ruins of a medieval church and some archaeological objects are on display. The building, which was built as the original city hall in the 19th century, is a remnant of the past. Also, being a library you can also borrow and read books, and it's the site of various events.

spots.name: Trampe
spots.summary: The world's first and only bike lift.

spots.name: Dora 1
spots.summary: The German submarine base for the 13th flotilla during the German occupation of Norway (1940 - 1945). Today the bunker houses several archives, among them are the Trondheim city archives, NTNU university and governmental archives.

photo.author: No 5 Army Film & Photographic Unit, Tanner (Lt)

spots.name: Antikvariatet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the most popular, yet laid-back bars in the city. Located in a historic wharf along Bakklandet and right around the corner from Gamle Bybru, they have moderately priced beer, as well as a selection of special brews. Often a good place to grab a cheap bite to eat if you get here early enough. This bar really captures the heart of Trøndersk community. You'll find a very diverse crowd: locals,

spots.name: Den Gode Nabo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Just across the Old Town bridge and down a scary-looking staircase, this is a brown fisherman's pub in an old warehouse. As atmospheric as it gets, they have Trondheim's most lovely outdoor seating in summer. The place is divided between the "grown-ups section" by the entrance, and the "student section" further in. Popular among students and all others and not too expensive if you prefer the regul

spots.name: Grafen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A café and bar with a varied menu of foods. The restaurant reinvented itself into Grafen and now serves up a luxurious Mediterranean-style offering rather than the more fast-food offering it previously had. It has dishes like steamed mussels. They have an extensive beer, wine and cocktail list (including local artisanal beers) and a quite popular place for just going out for a drink. It is best to

spots.name: Studentersamfundet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The red, roundhouse that previously housed the Trondheim Interrail centre during summer and the student society otherwise. The café Edgar serves decent food at a low cost. To get to Edgar, go in through the glass doors and up one floor. Lyche (entrance to the south) serves good food (the burgers are the most popular dish, but they also serve soups, fancier dinner options, and dessert) for just a f

spots.name: To Rom og Kjøkken

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The name is inspired by a tale about a tram driver on Gråkallbanen. The restaurant opened in 2005 and features a three to five-course menu starting at kr 545 and an à la carte menu with both fish and meat. Between opening at 16:00 and 18:00, they serve "Today's Bar special" for kr 169. The selection of dishes depends on the actual season and local production since they try to use as much local pro

spots.name: Egon Tårnet

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The rotating restaurant at the top of the Tyholt tv and Radio Tower, the tallest structure in Trondheim. Famous for their pizza buffet (everyday for people that arrive before 6pm), they also offer a vast menu of different options. There are other Egon restaurants around town as well, the most central being in Søndre gate, Prinsens gate and at the Solsiden mall.

spots.name: Cafe 3b

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 3b is an institution in Trondheim. Leading on in the "big beer war" of the -90's, it was dirt cheap for years. Now it's more expensive, but it's still an enjoyable, black hole catering for rock and indie kids of every denomination imaginable. Hip-hop kids have their own private dungeon down the corridor behind the bar in the basement.

spots.name: Kvilhaugen gård

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: If you venture out of the centre to get your beer, make it here. Wonderful outdoor seating with views of most of Trondheim. Inside, it's an old farmhouse with plenty of atmosphere. It's also a restaurant with mains from kr 150-300 from the à la carte menu as well as four different 3-course menus starting from around kr 550 per person.

spots.name: DownTown

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Near the crossing of Nordre gate and Fjordgata, it is widely known among students due to its pianobar. Cheap beer during the week (kr 19 for 33cl) and a lot of international students, especially on Thursday. According to their home page, the bar is closed for renovation as of September 2014.

spots.name: Fru Lundgreens

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In the basement of the concert hall, Fru Lundgreens looks like the inside of a lung but has good, cheap beer and a brilliant jukebox. Crowd is rock. Pool table in the back. Prices vary on time, but always good value. The food of the day is good if you need something with your beer.

spots.name: Trondhjem Mikrobryggeriet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A brewery pub offering a range of beer brewed in-house (about six kinds plus a seasonal special). Prices for a 0.5L about 50% higher than elsewhere, but the only place in town to offer an IPA and a bitter from tap - along with the other four. Substantial food is served, too.

spots.name: Bakklandet Skydsstation

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The place to find one of Trondheim's best seafood collections, such as a herring buffet and baccalao (dried or salted cod). The restaurant is quite small with around ten small tables, so you might want to come a bit outside regular dining times to get a seat.

spots.name: Carl Johan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The northernmost end of Nordre gate is the hub of Trondheim nightlife, with mainstream discos, sausage kiosks and lots of drunk, well-dressed people. Carl Johan is a straightforward pub with more relaxed ambience than most offerings in the area.

spots.name: Lille London
spots.summary: A pub that caters to a wide variety of people. They show football games live, and the second story has a billiards room with two pool tables. During the weekends there is often live music in the second story.

spots.name: Ramp

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This laid-back, organic restaurant is a good place to relax and play board games. It offers good food at good prices. Any eastbound bus will take you to Strandveien stop.

spots.name: Lager 11

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Street food hall and event center. Casual and inexpensive food is available from 8 different food stalls. Choices range from Greek, Mexican, and Vietnamese food.

spots.name: Tavern

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This 19th- and early 20th-century themed restaurant with decor from the 18th century serves a variety of central Norwegian food.
